Blepharitis

In 17 patients with Demodex-associated blepharitis, symptoms and ocular-surface measures improved after combined IPL and low-level light, with no adverse events reported. A rat study reported improved tear-related signs and lower inflammatory markers after 808 nm PBM.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In 17 patients with Demodex-associated blepharitis, symptoms and ocular-surface measures improved after combined IPL and low-level light, with no adverse events reported. A rat study reported improved tear-related signs and lower inflammatory markers after 808 nm PBM.

Summary of the Evidence

Two unique primary publications address blepharitis: one retrospective human series and one rat experiment. The human series combined intense pulsed light, or IPL, with low-level light, so it does not isolate PBM. No review or human PBM-only randomized trial was identified.

Human and clinical evidence

Farrant and colleagues reported 17 patients and 34 eyes with Demodex-associated blepharitis treated with combined IPL and low-level light. Symptoms and ocular-surface measures improved, and no treatment-related adverse events were reported. The retrospective design and combined intervention mean that neither the PBM-specific effect nor comparison with usual care can be determined (Farrant et al. 2025).

Animal evidence

Kim and colleagues used a rat ocular-surface model. Treatment with 808 nm near-infrared PBM improved tear and ocular signs, reduced inflammatory markers, and did not produce observed retinal damage. These findings are specific to the animal model and cannot establish patient benefit (Kim et al. 2021).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo study was identified. Inflammatory-marker measurements in the rat report are not separate cell experiments.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The human protocol paired blue light and red low-level light with IPL, with roughly 12 minutes per light component and a mean of 7.6 treatment sessions. The rat study used 808 nm near-infrared light. The species, device, diagnosis, and co-intervention differ, and the human series does not estimate the contribution of PBM apart from IPL.

Interpretation

The human report shows improvement after a combined clinic protocol, while the animal study supports biological activity in a model. A PBM-specific clinical effect remains uncertain because there is no controlled human comparison separating the light components.

Publications and records2 unique titles

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One small retrospective human series combined intense pulsed light with blue and red low-level light and had no separate PBM-only control. A rat model reported improved tear and inflammatory measures, but animal findings do not identify a clinical effect. A controlled human comparison that separates IPL from PBM is needed.
